newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down on price concern.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down on price concern.

text.p: Talk of reduced packer asking prices for cash bellies and an overbought market sparked liquidation that kept CME pork bellies limit down at the close. Hog futures followed with added pressure in deferreds linked to early projections for the USDA Hogs and Pigs report later this month, traders said.

Pork bellies closed down the 3.000-cent-per-lb daily limit in all months with July ending at 87.250 cents. Hog futures finished 0.200 to 1.825 cent lower with June off the least at 81.025 cents. December was off most after falling the 2.000-cent limit earlier.

Reports that packers reduced asking prices for cash bellies added to early long liquidation that was encouraged by continued resistance around 90 cents, basis July, and a technically overbought market, traders said.
"The trade is looking at the $90 area saying that everytime you see a rally back to $90 you see selling instead of buying support," said Jason Roose from U.S. Commodities.

Cash sources reported that packers lowered asking prices for cash bellies to the $88 to $89 per cwt level from $92 per cwt overnight. The seasonal trend for futures to invert, move to a discount to cash, added to the bearish tone, sources said.
"The reason we are down is that we need to have inversion," said Bill Cippola, belly trader for Iowa Grain.

E.D.&F. Man and Lind-Waldock notably sold into sell stops early. Further losses are seen Friday as options trade had July trading synthetically down 0.750 at 86.500 and August synthetically down 0.800 at 86.000 cents, pit sources said.

Hog futures also fell as profit taking weighed on nearby contracts. Also concern ahead of USDA's quarterly hog report this month weighed heavily on deferred months. Unwinding of bear spreads added to the trend for the nearby to hold and deferred months to move lower, traders said.

"At this stage, people are looking at the Hog and Pig report and it's getting close enough to the time frame now" that it starts to influence the market. "There's too much news out there telling us that there is going to be six percent more hogs," Roose said.

Rand Financials generally sold July and August early but bought July late. Dean Witter and ING bought July early. Rosenthal Collins and E.D.&F. Man sold deferred months into sell stops, pit sources said.
In hog options, First Chicago bought July 78 and 80 puts, pit sources added.
